profileName: SwissCRO — Composed Risk Leadership, Anti-Overpreparation & Boardroom Poise (B2–C1)

watchOuts.title: Slow the Pace Before You Answer Tense Pushback
watchOuts.detail: When a board or business-line leader challenges a risk call, rushing to defend your position amplifies internal tension. Buy yourself a calm 2-second breath, acknowledge the question neutrally ('That's the core trade-off we're weighing'), and speak 15% slower than the room.

watchOuts.title: Replace 20-Page Mental Scripts With Three Core Pillars
watchOuts.detail: Over-preparing creates fragility—the moment a meeting goes off-script, anxiety spikes. Anchor every topic to just three headlines (The Risk, The Impact, The Guardrail) so you can pivot effortlessly even when caught cold.

watchOuts.tag: Swiss-Banking Drift · Reclaiming Native US Crispness
watchOuts.title: Trimming 'Euro-Banking' Clutter After 20+ Years in Switzerland
watchOuts.detail: Two decades in Swiss banking naturally pulls German-influenced syntax and stiff phrasing into your English ('We have to take care about this topic', 'actual risk appetite'). Reclaim natural, idiomatic American directness: 'Here is where we draw the line' and 'Our current exposure sits at...'

watchOuts.title: Channeling a CRO's Vigilance Into Calm Authority
watchOuts.detail: Your instinct to anticipate what could go wrong is literally your superpower as a CRO—it only hurts when it sounds defensive. Present risks as clear, unemotional options ('If we take Path A, here is the capital buffer we need') rather than personal warnings.

watchOuts.title: Lowering Vocal Pitch at the Period Under Scrutiny
watchOuts.detail: Tension pushes vocal pitch upward and clips breath support. Drop your pitch cleanly at the end of every recommendation—signaling quiet, unshakeable executive certainty even if your pulse is up.

scenarios.title: Caught Cold in ExCo: Answering an Unscripted Risk Question Without Panicking
scenarios.prompt: Midway through an Executive Committee meeting, the CEO pivots to an emerging regulatory or credit issue you didn't prepare slides for. Use a calm 3-step bridge (Acknowledge → Frame what is known → State next verification step) in 45 seconds without apologizing for not having every number memorized.

scenarios.title: Holding Your Ground When Revenue Leaders Push Back on a Risk Limit
scenarios.prompt: A commercial division head argues in a heated meeting that your risk controls are slowing down a major deal. Respond with zero defensiveness—separating the person from the risk math and holding the line in four calm, measured sentences.

scenarios.title: The 'No-Notes' 60-Second Quarterly Risk Briefing
scenarios.prompt: Deliver a high-level quarterly risk summary using only three mental bullet points—no script, no exhaustive caveats. Practice trusting your 20+ years of banking instinct instead of over-explaining.

scenarios.title: Climbing an Alpine Pass on Two Wheels: Pacing Effort When the Gradient Spikes
scenarios.prompt: Tell a short story about pacing yourself up a steep Swiss climb or sport event—how staying smooth in the saddle beats fighting the gradient—and connect that physical composure to navigating tense boardroom debates.

scenarios.title: Chicago Roots Meet Swiss Precision: Unplugging on a Family Trip
scenarios.prompt: Share a favorite family holiday memory with your three kids where plans went sideways on the road—and how letting go of total control turned it into a great story. Keep the tone warm, humorous, and unhurried.

customCards.term: Caught-Cold Bridge: What do you say when asked an unexpected question in a tense meeting without sounding unprepared or defensive?
customCards.definition: "That's the right question to ask. Based on current exposures, here is the headline picture—and I'll confirm the exact stress-test figures by 2 PM."
customCards.example: Acknowledge the question, give your directional CRO judgment, and set a crisp follow-up time.
customCards.note: Anti-Overpreparation: Senior executives respect calm directional judgment far more than memorized spreadsheets.

customCards.term: Emotional Reset Cue: What physical and vocal reset stops tension from hijacking your delivery in a heated debate?
customCards.definition: Exhale fully before speaking, drop your shoulders, speak 15% slower than the person who just challenged you, and end your first sentence on a firm downward pitch.
customCards.example: "Let's step back and look at the downside exposure objectively."
customCards.note: Composure Under Pressure: Controlling your tempo forces the entire room's energy to slow down.

customCards.term: Swiss-Banking Drift Fix: "We need to take care about our actual liquidity buffer in case the market makes a big movement."
customCards.definition: "We need to stay disciplined on our current liquidity buffer in case markets swing sharply."
customCards.example: Reclaim natural US banking phrasing: 'current' (not Swiss/German 'actual') and 'stay disciplined on' (not 'take care about').
customCards.note: Native Crispness: Twenty years in Switzerland subtly imports German prepositions and false friends.

customCards.term: Holding the Line Without Heat: How do you push back on an aggressive business-line proposal without sounding emotional or rigid?
customCards.definition: "I understand the commercial upside—my responsibility is making sure one bad quarter doesn't wipe out three years of margin. Here is the structure that works."
customCards.example: Validate the commercial goal first, anchor your pushback in institutional protection, and offer a workable path.
customCards.note: Executive Gravitas: Calmly framing risk as stewardship removes personal friction.

customCards.term: Anti-Overpreparation Rule: Before walking into a high-stakes meeting, what is the maximum prep you allow yourself?
customCards.definition: Write down exactly three headlines on one index card: 1) Core Risk, 2) Worst-Case Impact, 3) Recommended Guardrail—then close the notebook.
customCards.example: When you know your three pillars cold, you never lose your place when interrupted.
customCards.note: Structural Confidence: Less script equals more agility under live questioning.

customCards.term: Reframing Worry: "I'm really worried that if we approve this credit line, we could face serious regulatory trouble later."
customCards.definition: "Approving this credit line without tighter covenants exposes us to clear regulatory scrutiny—here is how we close that gap upfront."
customCards.example: Shift from 'I'm worried...' (personal emotion) to 'This exposes us to...' (objective CRO analysis).
customCards.note: Tone Shift: Objective risk framing turns anxiety into quiet boardroom authority.
